description: Just as Canopus has guided explorers across unknown horizons, Our team aspires to illuminate new paths in planetary research. We believe every discovery begins with curiosity, and every great journey begins with a vision.
summary: We built Rehearsal Sites, a web tool that helps mission teams choose where on Earth to rehearse a Moon or Mars mission. The user picks a target (the lunar south pole, a lunar lava-tube pit, Jezero, Gale or Arcadia Planitia) and a job to practice, such as ice drilling, rover mobility, power, habitat thermal testing or cave exploration. The tool ranks 16 Earth sites on a map using eight traits, including cold, dryness, ice, terrain, volcanic rock, low-sun light, caves and thin air. It adds a sun-angle match for the chosen month and lists where each site falls short. It also flags five under-studied sites as candidates for new analogs. A Python pipeline computes trait values from NASA POWER, NASADEM, planetary orbit data and LRO, MOLA and Odyssey measurements. This matters because the best test site depends on the job, and analog sites are rarely compared with Moon and Mars targets in a clear, explainable way.
details: Team Canopus Nova built Rehearsal Sites, a browser-based tool that helps mission teams choose where on Earth to rehearse for a Moon or Mars base. The user picks a target (lunar south pole, lunar lava-tube pit, Jezero, Gale or Arcadia Planitia) and a job to practice, such as ice drilling, rover mobility, power, habitat thermal testing or caves. The app scores 16 Earth sites, including Atacama, Death Valley, Haughton Crater and the McMurdo Dry Valleys, on eight traits (cold, dryness, ice, terrain, volcanic rock, low-sun light, caves and thin air). It weights the traits by the chosen job, adds a sun-angle match for the selected month, and shows a map, a ranked list and the gaps where each site falls short. It also flags five under-studied sites as candidates for new analogs. We wrote it in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a Python pipeline designed to compute trait values from NASA POWER, NASADEM, planetary orbit data and LRO, MOLA and Odyssey measurements, and we built it with help from Claude. It is creative because it ranks by mission job, not one generic score, and it states what Earth cannot replicate. We considered data limits, such as the coarse NASA POWER grid, and the app reports how many values come from NASA data and how many are estimates. The intended impact is clearer, more transparent analog-site selection for future missions.
